sources.title: Deterministic OpenJDK 21 product-pairs fixture and brute-force oracle

claims.text: The preserved source asks for all pairs whose product equals target and shows value pairs, but does not specify index-pair multiplicity, duplicate-output policy, ordering, zero handling or negative-value constraints. The candidate therefore labels unique normalized value-pair semantics as an explicit answer contract rather than source fact.

Under the explicit unique-value-pair contract, the executable Java fixture validates the source example, duplicate/same-value requirements, negative values, zero-target behavior, integer-division boundary handling, null/single inputs, and 500 deterministic random arrays against a brute-force index-pair oracle reduced to unique normalized value pairs.
